general.temas: The election campaign dominates the front pages, with attention on the PSOE’s platform, opinion polls and proposals on housing and care. Also featuring repeatedly are the attack during a PP event in Hernani, migrant arrivals on El Hierro and the Spain-England match. Only Público highlights the outsourcing to consultants and lawyers of the drafting of tender documents for contracts at Madrid hospitals.
general.motivo_crispacion: The campaign features intense confrontation between parties, with accusations and polarizing statements about immigration and racism. The attack during a PP event in Hernani adds to tensions and prompts Feijóo to reproach Sánchez and his allies. There are also disagreements over housing, regional financing and social rights, alongside highly critical headlines. By contrast, sports and cultural news, such as Sergio Ramírez’s induction into the RAE, provide less contentious subjects.

El País.resumen:
- The PSOE presents proposals on housing, child-rearing, taxes and energy; a poll examines its electoral support.
- Feijóo will campaign in Gipuzkoa after an attack on young PP members; Abascal links immigration and crime using false data.
- The front page covers young first-time voters, electoral preferences in Sigüés and a television appearance by Sánchez.
- Sergio Ramírez is inducted into the RAE and Spain faces England in the Nations League.
- Other stories cover victims of bank fraud and the downfall of Jensen Huang in a case involving alleged espionage and adultery.
El País.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although phrases such as “vulture funds,” “the victims’ ordeal” and “glory and downfall” add an emotional and sensationalist charge.
El País.sesgo: The front page gives particular prominence to the PSOE and the election campaign, with several pieces on its proposals and support. It also takes a notably critical approach to Vox by comparing a claim by Abascal with statistics.

El Mundo.resumen:
- The PP and Vox would together win 51% of the vote and up to 199 seats, with the PSOE stalled.
- Sánchez presents election proposals on friendship and regional financing; Colau proposes leave to care for people close to the employee.
- Feijóo reproaches Sánchez over the attack on the PP candidate in Gipuzkoa; young Vox voters discuss Abascal’s absence from an event.
- The front page highlights the arrival of thousands of migrants on El Hierro and a housing event held by the Tenants’ Union.
- In sports, the standouts are Real Madrid’s basketball victory and Zverev’s win over Jódar; the pope’s visit to Cusco is also covered.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Phrases such as “El Hierro trembles,” “steals” votes and “Abascal’s no-show” add alarm and drama, although other headlines are descriptive.
El Mundo.sesgo: The selection prioritizes the electoral contest and uses language critical of proposals from the PSOE and Frente Amplio, while also presenting immigration in an alarmist light. It also includes criticism of Abascal, so there is no apparent uniform orientation across all the headlines.

ABC.resumen:
- Sánchez proposes enshrining protections for abortion, pensions and housing in the Constitution; the PSOE’s platform includes child-rearing measures and labor reforms.
- The front page includes criticism of Sánchez, including over his comments about Abascal and the government’s relationship with Morocco.
- Feijóo announces an event with Jon Echeverría after an event was canceled because of stone-throwing.
- The front page reviews De la Espriella’s first hundred days in Colombia and Leo XIV’s trip to Cusco.
- The front page includes Sergio Ramírez’s induction into the RAE and news about soccer, basketball and tennis.
ABC.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines appear alongside judgmental or alarmist phrases such as “populist ceremony,” “runaway debt” and “is falling to pieces,” the last attributed to García Albiol.
ABC.sesgo: A critical approach to Sánchez and the PSOE is evident both in the selection of stories and in editorial language questioning their proposals and style. The front page also includes criticism from PP leaders, although it is presented as attributed statements.

Público.resumen:
- Madrid hospitals commission external consultants and lawyers to draft tender documents for contracts.
- The left seeks to mobilize voters with proposals on family diversity, feminism and LGBTQ+ rights.
- The PSOE proposes taxes on funds and big tech companies and more spending on housing; Frente Amplio proposes leave for “chosen family.”
- Several headlines carry statements and analysis on political confrontation and the left’s electoral prospects.
- Other stories address the bailout of Galicia’s savings banks and matters related to Núcleo Nacional, Altsasu and Congress.
Público.motivo_populismo: Confrontational and emotionally charged phrases abound, such as “sucks up fascism,” “wanting slaves,” “inquisitor,” “vulture funds” and “techno-oligarchs,” although other headlines have an informative tone.
Público.sesgo: The front page pays particular attention to the left’s proposals and social rights, with a critical approach to the right and certain economic actors. Several formulations and quotations reinforce a confrontational reading of politics.

OKdiario.resumen:
- A young man renovates two sheds to turn them into a home for his mother.
- Inda responds to Pedro Sánchez with accusations about the AVE high-speed rail system and stolen money; another story contrasts Feijóo’s attendance at a soccer match with Sánchez’s television appearance.
- The Spain-England match features in several stories, including Pubill’s injury and the tribute to Jesús de Miguel and the victims of the Urda accident.
- El Hierro receives 1,261 immigrants in seven cayucos over the course of one day.
- Other stories address a Bob Dylan quote, people who speak loudly and the reintroduction of donkeys into the desert.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: The confrontation and accusations of “your dead” and “the money you have stolen” stand out, as do the disparaging description “to whitewash his image” and sensationalist formulations such as “Nobody saw it coming.”
OKdiario.sesgo: The front page shows an approach favorable to Feijóo and critical of Sánchez, contrasting the former’s support for Spain with a disparaging description of the latter’s television appearance. It also devotes ample space to soccer and human-interest content.

opiniones.comunista:
Housing is back at the center of the campaign, and rightly so. I see the PSOE’s proposal to devote 1% of GDP to social housing and tax speculation as recognition of the problem, but not a sufficient solution. As long as land and housing remain, above all, assets for generating rental income, the right to a home will depend on the interests of big capital. We need a large, permanent stock of public housing, alongside forms of collective ownership under democratic control. The Tenants’ Union’s mobilization points to the strength needed to demand it.

I am also concerned that Madrid hospitals are outsourcing the drafting of contracts to external consultants and law firms. Public services need their own capabilities and sufficient staff, not growing dependence on private companies. The class struggle is also being fought over who makes decisions about shared resources.
opiniones.anarquista:
Housing is back in the campaign: the PSOE promises to devote 1% of GDP to it, and the Tenants’ Union is mobilizing to keep the crisis from disappearing from the debate. I do not dismiss any improvement that brings relief to those who cannot afford rent, but I distrust leaving a right at the mercy of governments, budgets and landlords. I prefer a neighborhood movement strong enough to decide and collectively manage where and how people live, without waiting for permission from the parties.

I also reject linking immigration and crime with false data. Turning those who arrive into scapegoats divides people who could defend their needs together. Freedom is not just about choosing a ballot: it requires mutual aid, autonomy and real power in the face of those who concentrate wealth and authority.
opiniones.liberal:
Housing deserves solutions, not just spending announcements. I am concerned that the PSOE proposes devoting 1% of GDP to social housing and adding a tax on large property owners: taxing investment could reduce the supply we need. I would rather make it easier to build, speed up permits and protect legal certainty so that more people can choose where to live.

I also welcome the PP’s proposal to exempt earnings from personal income tax during the first year of a first job, although I would aspire to a broader and more lasting reduction. Earning a salary should allow people to keep more of the fruits of their own labor, not become increasingly dependent on benefits. A limited state should protect rights and help those in need, but without replacing personal responsibility or turning every difficulty into an excuse to raise taxes.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see the arrivals on El Hierro as proof that Spain needs to regain effective control of its borders. A strict immigration policy, with swift procedures and respect for the law, protects both sovereignty and our communities’ capacity to receive people. There is no need for false figures to defend it: they weaken a cause that must be grounded in truth.

I am also concerned about the attack during the campaign in Hernani. No idea should be imposed through stones or intimidation; political freedom must be defended for everyone.

Rather than promises of more spending and taxes, I would prefer to make it easier for young people to work, start a family and find a home. Elites can wrap their programs in flags and TV sets, but patriotism is demonstrated by guaranteeing security, equality among Spaniards and the continuity of our traditions.
opiniones.centro:
I believe devoting more resources to social housing and supporting child-rearing are reasonable goals: a prosperous economy must also offer opportunities to those who start with less. But the PSOE’s commitment to devote 1% of GDP to housing requires an explanation of how it will be financed and how it will increase supply. Taxing speculation can be useful if it is well designed; it must not replace cooperation with the private sector or become an obstacle to building.

I am also concerned about the deterioration of public debate. The attack during the campaign in Hernani deserves unequivocal condemnation: everyone must be able to defend their ideas freely. And linking immigration and crime with false data, as Abascal has done regarding Cornellà, solves no problem. In response to the arrivals on El Hierro, I prefer institutional cooperation, sufficient resources and an orderly immigration policy that respects human dignity.
